ATK: Attack time: how quickly the envelope rises after a note starts.
DEC: Decay time from the attack peak to the sustain level.
SUS: Sustain level while the key or gate remains held; this is a level, not a time.
REL: Release time after key-up; longer tails continue to consume voices.
PIT: Pitch or pitch modulation depth. In an envelope/LFO destination page this is an amount, not a tuning reference.
PITCH: Pitch or pitch modulation depth. In an envelope/LFO destination page this is an amount, not a tuning reference.
FLT: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
FENV: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
ENV: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
SHP: Waveform/timbre shaping or the amount of envelope/LFO shaping, according to this page.
SHAPE: Waveform/timbre shaping or the amount of envelope/LFO shaping, according to this page.
RATE: Speed of the selected oscillator/modulator/effect. The displayed unit identifies Hz or a tempo division.
WAVE: Select the oscillator or modulation waveform. Changing the shape changes its harmonic content or movement.
WAVE2: Select the oscillator or modulation waveform. Changing the shape changes its harmonic content or movement.
FADE: Time for LFO modulation to fade in after a note starts.
AMP: Amplitude modulation depth. Start with a small amount to avoid large level swings.
VEL>F: Velocity-to-filter sensitivity; stronger key strikes change brightness.
MW>: Destination controlled by the MIDI modulation wheel.
AT>: Destination controlled by MIDI channel pressure/aftertouch.
SRC: Modulation source for the selected matrix slot.
DST: Modulation destination for the selected matrix slot; engine targets follow the current engine.
AMT: Depth of the selected modulation connection or processor. Bipolar ranges reverse the effect below zero.
SLOT: Select the item being edited; on PROGRAM this is the saved program slot, on MATRIX it is one of the 12 modulation connections.
LANE: Select one of four modulation sequencer lanes.
STEP: Choose the modulation-sequencer step to edit.
VALUE: Set the selected step value, or the exact MIDI CC value required by a pedal assignment.
LEN: Length of the current sequence or setlist. Shorter lengths wrap sooner; a setlist length of zero disables the list.
LENGTH: Length of the current sequence or setlist. Shorter lengths wrap sooner; a setlist length of zero disables the list.
SMTH: Smooth transitions between modulation-sequencer step values.
SYNC: Clock/synchronization source. External sync requires a running clock on the selected input.
CHOR: Chorus amount/send; adds detuned movement and width.
CHO: Chorus amount/send; adds detuned movement and width.
FILT: Part or master DJ-style filter: negative is low-pass, zero OFF, positive high-pass.
INSRT: Select the per-part insert processor; its three following controls change with the type.
INS A: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
INS B: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
INS C: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
MIX: Dry/wet balance or shared effect output level, as identified by the page.
TIME: Delay time. Listen for pitch changes when changing tape-style delay time.
FDBK: Feedback/recirculation. High values prolong the effect and can greatly increase level.
FB: Feedback/recirculation. High values prolong the effect and can greatly increase level.
COLR: Tone or spectral balance of this sound/processor.
TONE: Tone or spectral balance of this sound/processor.
TYPE: Select an effect or MIDI-message type.
DAMP: High-frequency damping; darker reverberation or faster high-frequency decay as raised.
PRE: Reverb pre-delay before the reverberant tail.
LOW: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
MID: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
HIGH: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
COMP: Master bus compression amount; compare at similar listening volume.
ROOT: Root note of the selected scale. This transposes the scale relationship; it does not transpose every played note.
SCL: Keyboard scale used by note quantization and scale-aware chords.
QNT: OFF leaves note selection chromatic; SNAP moves notes to the chosen scale; WHITE maps white-key playing into that scale. ALL modes apply the setting across all four parts and MIDI input.
CHORD: Chord generator voicing. OFF plays individual notes. Available voicings are filtered for compatibility with the active microtonal scale.
TRN: Transpose this part by semitones; octave shifts are multiples of 12.
TRANS: Transpose this part by semitones; octave shifts are multiples of 12.
STRUM: Spread chord notes in time. The upper values select tempo-synchronized direction/rate combinations.
VCE: Part voice mode: POLY, MONO, LEG, UNI, UNI2 or UNI4. Unison consumes additional voices from the shared budget.
MODEL: Select the filter model exposed by this engine. The capability map determines which controls actually operate.
F1 MODEL: Select the filter model exposed by this engine. The capability map determines which controls actually operate.
CUT: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
F1 CUT: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
LPF: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
RES: Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation.
F1 RES: Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation.
Q: Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation.
DRIVE: Drive into a saturation/filter stage. More drive can add harmonics and change level.
DRV: Drive into a saturation/filter stage. More drive can add harmonics and change level.
TRIM: Sound output calibration in half-dB steps. This changes the sound gain independently of the part mixer level.
VOIC: Chord voicing: CLOSE, SMOOTH, OPEN, INV1, INV2 or +OCT. This changes the layout of generated chord notes, not the part polyphony.
GLMOD: Choose which note transitions use glide.
PRIO: Priority of held notes in a monophonic part.
ALLOC: Voice allocation/unison setting. Extra voices consume the shared eight-voice budget.
DTUNE: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
DTUN: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
DTN: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
VINTG: Vintage variation/drift; adds small imperfections rather than changing the scale.
SPRED: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
SPRD: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
WIDTH: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
BPM: Internal tempo in beats per minute.
SWING: Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions.
SWG: Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions.
TUNE: Select the master tuning system, including maqam and custom/Scala options.
FROM: On TUNING, select the lowest affected octave C0-C8. Notes below it remain equal temperament. On FMX ROUTE, choose the source operator.
MASTER: Apply master tuning to the selected part; ON by default. OFF bypasses the shared maqam/microtuning for that part.
A4: Reference frequency of A4, in Hz. This is separate from the tuning-system octave boundary.
MIDI: Enable/route sequencer MIDI output according to the listed modes.
IN CH: Accepted MIDI input channel; OMNI accepts all channels, subject to the controller protocol/MPE settings.
OUT: On MIDI: output channel. On FMX ROUTE: selected operator output level.
BEND: Pitch-bend range in semitones; AUTO follows supported configuration messages.
LOCAL: Whether the onboard keyboard drives the internal synth. MIDI input remains a separate path.
EWI: Breath-controller handling: OFF, volume, or volume plus pressure behavior.
KEY IN: Choose USB, TRS or both for keyboard MIDI input.
PORT: MIDI transport/cable selection; AUTO uses automatic controller cable selection where offered.
ACTION: Select the pedal action to learn, edit or test.
LEARN: Arm MIDI learn. Press the pedal once, inspect the captured message, then accept it.
ACCEPT: Commit the captured MIDI message to the selected pedal action.
DUP ms: Duplicate-message suppression window in milliseconds. Zero disables suppression; use the smallest useful window so intentional taps remain distinct.
NUMBER: MIDI CC number or program-change number for this assignment.
CH: Assignment channel. IN CH follows the configured input channel; numbered choices match that channel specifically.
USB ROLE: COMPUTER enables device/editor operation; PEDAL enables USB host operation. Stop notes/playback before changing roles and use powered host hardware.
SCENE: Choose one of four compact scenes within the working program.
CAPTURE: Store the current supported mix, mutes, sends, macros and tuning settings into the selected scene.
RECALL: Apply the selected captured scene without loading another program.
ENTRY: Choose the position to edit in the ordered setlist.
PROGRAM: Assign a saved program number to this setlist position.
LOAD: Load the selected saved program/setlist entry. Storage actions require their on-screen confirmation.
ON: Enable this part in layered playback.
SPLIT: Enable keyboard-range filtering for this part.
UPPER: OFF uses the lower side, including the boundary. ON uses notes above the boundary.
POINT: Split boundary as a MIDI note number. The held EDIT mixer presents it as a note/octave name.
LEVEL: Level of the selected part/operator/processor; use the page context to identify which one. A zero part level silences that part.
PAN: Position of the selected part in the stereo field; center is zero.
MUTE: Silence the selected part without deleting its sound.
SOLO: Hear the soloed part(s), subject to layer routing/enabled state.
LAYER: Toggle four-part performance. OFF plays the focused part; ON uses enabled parts and their routing.
NAME: Edit the selected saved-program name. ALGORITHM chooses a character position; PRESET/KNOB 2 changes its character.
SAVE: Write the working four-part program to the selected saved slot after confirmation.
CLRSQ: Clear sequence data using the requested confirmation; this is destructive to the working pattern.
INIT: Initialize the selected working sound. Save a copy before using it.
NEW: Initialize the working project/program as requested by the confirmation. Back up wanted edits first.
MODE: Choose the operating mode for this page: LFO restart, arp direction, delay style, controller protocol or operator frequency mode.
OCT: Arpeggiator octave range or part octave shift, depending on the page.
GATE: Duration of each generated arp/sequence note as a fraction of its step.
PROB: Probability of playing a generated note. Lower settings deliberately omit some notes.
HOLD: Keep the arpeggiated/held notes after key-up. Turn off to release the latched note set.
ORD: Order in which held notes enter the arpeggiator.
SPICE: Amount of controlled variation applied to generated notes.
DICE: Variation seed/reroll control. TURNG mode changes its interpretation to a repeating random sequence seed.
LOOP: Repeat/loop behavior. On ENV 2, ONE is a single contour and LOOP repeats it; on SPICE/TURNG it repeats generated variation.
DIV: Pattern step division relative to tempo.
MOD: On MOD PRESET, choose a ready-made expressive routing; other pages use it for modulation amount.
APPLY: Apply the selected modulation template. Existing required slots are checked before changing routings.
OP: Select one of the six FMX operators to edit.
RATIO: Operator frequency ratio relative to the played note.
FINE: Fine operator tuning within the selected ratio.
VEL: Velocity sensitivity of the operator/modulation target.
KSC: Keyboard scaling of the selected operator level.
FREQ: Fixed-versus-ratio frequency behavior for the selected FMX operator.
ALG: FM/operator connection algorithm. Each choice changes which oscillators modulate or reach the output.
BITS: Bit depth of the crusher. Lower settings add quantization distortion.
HPF: High-pass cutoff; reduce unwanted low-frequency energy.
SUB: Sub-oscillator level under the main oscillator.
PW: Pulse width/duty cycle; changes harmonic balance.
DUTY: Pulse width/duty cycle; changes harmonic balance.
OSC2: Second oscillator setting/level. Use the engine description to distinguish oscillator type from mix.
HARM: Harmonic content/structure of the selected model.
POS: Position in a sample, wavetable, wave sequence or excitation, as indicated by the engine.
START: Position in a sample, wavetable, wave sequence or excitation, as indicated by the engine.
TABL: Select the wavetable. USER WT remains silent until a user table is uploaded.
VOWL: Formant/vowel position; moving it changes the vocal resonance.
VOWL2: Formant/vowel position; moving it changes the vocal resonance.
16': Organ drawbar level for the indicated pitch register.
8': Organ drawbar level for the indicated pitch register.
4': Organ drawbar level for the indicated pitch register.
DENS: Grain density; more overlapping grains make a denser texture.
BOW: Bowing/excitation behavior of the physical model.
IDX: FM/phase modulation index; higher values generally add sidebands.
INT2: Pitch interval for the additional oscillator/voice in the trio.
INT3: Pitch interval for the additional oscillator/voice in the trio.
LPG: Low-pass gate behavior of the model.
X: Coordinate in the vector/terrain mix; moving between sources changes the timbre.
Y: Coordinate in the vector/terrain mix; moving between sources changes the timbre.
MRPH: Morph amount between the model waveforms.
KTR: Keyboard tracking: changes the filter/model response with played pitch.
KTRK: Keyboard tracking: changes the filter/model response with played pitch.
M1: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M2: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M3: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M4: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
A: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
B: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
C: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
D: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
SWP: Sweep amount or rate of the selected engine.
ARP: Engine-specific arpeggiation/model control; the dedicated ARP menu remains the performance arpeggiator.
CPU: CPU/engine implementation mode indicated by this model.
-: Unused control position; turning this knob has no assigned sound parameter on this layout.
--: Unused control position; turning this knob has no assigned sound parameter on this layout.
